input.command:
git add src/cache/store.rs && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption from concurrent tool installations

The CacheStore wrote content and metadata files with plain fs::write(),
which is not atomic. When multiple bivvy processes ran simultaneously
(e.g., parallel tool installations), readers could observe partially-
written files or metadata/content mismatches.

Two changes fix this:
- Writes now go through atomic_write() (write to temp file + rename),
  so readers never see incomplete data.
- load() treats unreadable or unparseable metadata as a cache miss
  (returns None) instead of propagating errors, making it resilient
  to any leftover corruption from before this fix.
EOF
)" 2>&1

input.command:
git add src/cache/store.rs && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption from concurrent tool installations

The CacheStore wrote content and metadata files with plain fs::write(),
which is not atomic. When multiple bivvy processes ran simultaneously
(e.g., parallel tool installations), readers could observe partially-
written files or metadata/content mismatches.

Two changes fix this:
- Writes now go through atomic_write() (write to temp file + rename),
  so readers never see incomplete data.
- load() treats unreadable or unparseable metadata as a cache miss
  (returns None) instead of propagating errors, making it resilient
  to any leftover corruption from before this fix.
EOF
)" 2>&1

input.command:
git add src/cache/store.rs && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption from concurrent tool installations

The CacheStore wrote content and metadata files with plain fs::write(),
which is not atomic. When multiple bivvy processes ran simultaneously
(e.g., parallel tool installations), readers could observe partially-
written files or metadata/content mismatches.

Two changes fix this:
- Writes now go through atomic_write() (write to temp file + rename),
  so readers never see incomplete data.
- load() treats unreadable or unparseable metadata as a cache miss
  (returns None) instead of propagating errors, making it resilient
  to any leftover corruption from before this fix.
EOF
)" 2>&1
